summary: SWE-Bench ProMax is a 170-instance refactoring benchmark mined from post-January-2025 'refactor' commits in 70 GitHub repositories across seven languages (26 Java instances from 11 repos), with expert-rewritten problem statements and manually pruned test suites. Six frontier/open-weight models are run under mini-swe-agent and OpenHands; the best resolve rate is 41.2% (GPT-5.2, OpenHands), and the main failure mode is agents editing too few files.

claims.claim: Best model achieves only 41.2% resolve rate; benchmark is unsaturated.
claims.evidence: Table 3: GPT-5.2 under OpenHands 41.2%; next Claude Sonnet 4.6 38.8%. Single run per model/scaffold, no variance.

claims.claim: Instances are large: 11.4 modified source files and 261.6 LOC on average.
claims.evidence: Table 2 dataset statistics (11.4 files, 261.6 LOC source gold patch; 15.9 total files incl. tests); Table 5 per language (Java 20.8 files avg).

claims.claim: Expert curation removes overly narrow/broad tests and yields descriptions that are necessary and sufficient for the gold patch.
claims.evidence: Stage 3 process described (§3.2) but no annotator count, no inter-rater agreement, no audit of residual test defects, and LLMs assisted rewriting (LLM usage disclosure). Quality is asserted, not measured.

claims.claim: Open-weight models are competitive at a fraction of the cost (GLM-5 36.5% at $0.24 vs Sonnet 4.6 38.8% at $4.77).
claims.evidence: Table 3 OpenHands rows. Differences of 2-5 pp on n=170 with single runs are not shown to be significant.

claims.claim: Dominant failure mode is incomplete cross-file propagation: agents modify fewer files than the gold patch.
claims.evidence: Figure 5 CDFs for two models (Sonnet 4.6, Kimi-K2.5) only; qualitative manual inspection, no quantified failure taxonomy.

patterns.note: New SWE-bench-family benchmark targeting multi-file refactoring with curated tests.
Resolution judged by full test-suite execution in prebuilt Docker containers.
Scaffold matters a lot: GPT-5.2 goes 21.8% (mini-swe-agent, bash-centric) to 41.2% (OpenHands, structured tools); Gemini-3-Pro gets worse (26.5% to 19.4%).
Problem statements rewritten as precise, self-contained specs stating components, transformation and invariants; argued (not ablated) to be necessary for fair evaluation.
Cost/resolve data (GLM-5 at ~1/20 the cost of Sonnet 4.6) is input to model-routing decisions but no routing is evaluated.
Incomplete propagation to peripheral call sites is exactly the gap deterministic codemods/recipes cover; not evaluated.

methodology.sample: 170 instances from 70 repos (29,782 candidates); per language 20-29 instances; TypeScript from only 2 repos, Rust from 5; Java 26 instances / 11 repos.
methodology.baselines: No prior-method baselines (benchmark paper); compares six models x two scaffolds with 300-step / $10 caps.
methodology.models: Gemini-3-Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.2, GLM-5, Kimi-K2.5, Qwen3.5.
methodology.variance: Single Pass@1 run per configuration; no CIs. Per-language rates rest on ~20-29 instances each.
methodology.contamination_controls: Commits after January 2025 only; no check against model training cutoffs, no decontamination analysis despite citing contamination as a motivation.
methodology.languages: Python, Java, TypeScript, Go, C, C++, Rust.

standards.artifacts: Dataset on Hugging Face (swe-bench-promax/SWE-Bench-ProMax) with Docker environments built via SWE-Factory; agent trajectories/scripts release not stated.

biases.detail: Single run per model/scaffold; model rankings separated by 2-5 pp on 170 instances; per-language cells of 20-29 instances swing widely (e.g. Gemini TypeScript 14.3% vs 0.0% across scaffolds).
Public GitHub commits from 2025 onward; several evaluated models likely trained after some commits; no cutoff-aware split.

Commits are selected by 'refactor' keyword and must change tests; some instances (e.g. PlantUML Gantt hour-level resolution, Appendix C.2) are feature changes, so 'behavior-preserving refactoring' is not consistently what is measured.
Curation quality (narrow/broad tests removed, descriptions sufficient) is asserted without annotator counts, agreement statistics, or an independent audit.
Per-language conclusions ('GLM-5 leads on Java 34.6%') rest on 26 Java instances = ~9 resolved tasks.

coi.affiliations: Affiliations not present in extracted text or metadata (15 authors). Funding: National Key R&D Program of China, Natural Science Foundation of Shanghai, Hong Kong RGC GRF and Theme-based Research Scheme.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Third-party models and open-source scaffolds; authors do not ship a ranked system.
coi.detail: No vendor affiliation identifiable; benchmark authors do not appear to rank their own system. Affiliation could not be verified from the text.

verdict_reason: Useful multilingual (incl. Java) large-patch refactoring benchmark at a peer-reviewed venue with released data, but curation quality is asserted rather than measured, no variance, no limitations section, weak contamination control, and small per-language cells.
applicability: Relevant as evidence that cross-file propagation is the main failure mode for agents on large changes: for the Java ingestion team, multi-file refactors (e.g. a content-schema change rippling through 4+ ingestion repos and delivery APIs) should not be trusted to a single agent pass. Harness implications: (1) after an agent edit, run a deterministic 'all call sites updated' check (compiler, grep/LSP references, OpenRewrite recipe where possible) before tests; (2) specs for refactors should enumerate affected components and invariants, as the benchmark's rewritten descriptions do; (3) scaffold choice moves results ~2x, so evaluate harnesses per host rather than assuming model rank transfers across Cursor/Claude Code/Codex. Java subset (26 instances, 11 repos) is a usable but small internal eval seed. Note it is single-repo per task, so it says nothing directly about cross-repo coordination.

conflicts_with.detail: SWE-Bench Pro Verified also re-curates benchmark tests; both claim to fix SWE-bench test-quality defects with different curation methods, so 'reliable' benchmark claims should be compared.
